preconditions.description: The input is a single integer n where 1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5.

postconditions.expression: (stdout.strip() == 'NO') or (stdout.strip() == 'YES' and all(line.split() in [['a', '+', 'b', '=', 'c'], ['a', '-', 'b', '=', 'c'], ['a', '*', 'b', '=', 'c']] for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:]))
postconditions.description: If it is impossible to obtain 24, output is exactly 'NO'. If possible, the first line is 'YES', followed by exactly n-1 lines of valid operations in the form 'a op b = c', where op is '+', '-', or '*', and c is the result of the operation (|c| ≤ 10^18). The final result of the operations must be 24.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in [int(num) for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:] for num in line.split() if num.isdigit()]) if stdout.strip() == 'YES' else True
postconditions.description: All numbers in operations (a, b, c) must be integers between 1 and n (inclusive) at the time of their use, except for intermediate results c which may exceed n but must satisfy |c| ≤ 10^18.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'YES' and eval(''.join([line.split('=')[1].strip() for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:]])) == 24 if stdout.strip() == 'YES' else True
postconditions.description: If 'YES' is printed, the sequence of operations must reduce the initial sequence [1, 2, ..., n] to exactly 24 through valid arithmetic operations.
